    Common questions

    Quick answers

    Straight answers to the questions customers ask first. The full list is on our FAQ page.

    Does the price include delivery?

    Guide prices on our Prices & Guides page exclude delivery and tax. Your quote is different: it's one all-in delivered price for your site, with delivery and tax worked out per job, because both depend on where the item lands.

    Can you find a specific machine or trailer for me?

    Yes — that's the job. Tell us the make, model, size, and budget you're working with, and we search dealer lots, auctions, and private sellers across Canada. Atlantic supply is thin, so the right unit often comes from Ontario or Quebec — we handle the hauling.

    Do you rent as well as sell?

    Yes, across the lines: containers rent month to month, equipment rents by the day, week, or month through established rental fleets, and trailer rentals can be arranged for moves, cleanups, and job sites.

    Container conditions explained

    Know what you're buying

    Container grades, in plain language — so the unit that arrives matches what you expected.

    Wind & watertight (used)

    A retired shipping container that still seals out wind and rain. Surface rust and dents are normal. The workhorse choice for storage — and the best value per square foot.

    Cargo-worthy (used)

    A used unit certified sound enough to ship cargo by sea. Structurally stronger than a basic storage grade — the grade to ask for if the container itself is travelling.

    One-trip (near-new)

    A container that has made a single loaded trip from the factory. Minimal wear, clean interior, current colours — the closest thing to new, for sites where appearance matters.

    Good to know

    Prices move — quotes don't

    Container prices move with steel and the US dollar, and used equipment moves with the auction market, so treat the figures above as guides. The price in your quote is the price you pay — one all-in delivered number, confirmed before any money changes hands.

    Before the truck arrives

    Getting your site ready

    A few practical things that make delivery day smooth.

    • Clear, level ground. A tilt-bed truck needs a firm, reasonably level spot and room to tilt and slide a container or shed off. Soft or sloped ground can need blocks or gravel — tell us about your site when you ask for a quote.

    • Check your local rules first. Charlottetown restricts storage containers on residential lots, and nearby municipalities allow them only as temporary ~60-day storage. Sheds have their own setback and permit rules in most towns. Ask us and we'll help you check before you commit.

    • Winter weather can move a date. The Confederation Bridge closes to high-sided vehicles 8–12 times a winter for wind. If your delivery is booked on one of those days, we'll reschedule at no extra charge.

    • Delivered prices are quoted per job. Distance, site access, and the Confederation Bridge crossing all move the number — a machine hauled from Ontario costs more to land than a local trailer. That's exactly why we quote one all-in price instead of posting a delivery chart.

    Delivery areas

    Six provinces, covered

    We deliver containers, equipment, trailers, and sheds across Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Newfoundland & Labrador, and Prince Edward Island. One all-in price, quoted for your exact site.

    Ontario

    Deliveries across Ontario for construction, farm, and commercial customers — from Ottawa and the east to Toronto, Hamilton, and beyond. Ontario is also where much of our equipment sourcing happens, so machines often ship direct to you.

    Quebec

    Regular deliveries across Quebec, including the Montreal and Quebec City regions, for job sites, farms, and businesses.

    Nova Scotia

    Regular deliveries across Nova Scotia — Halifax and the mainland, Cape Breton, and everywhere in between.

    New Brunswick

    Deliveries across New Brunswick — Moncton, Saint John, Fredericton, and rural sites province-wide.

    Newfoundland & Labrador

    Deliveries arranged to Newfoundland & Labrador, coordinated with ferry schedules — ask us for timing when you request your quote.

    Prince Edward Island

    Our home base. Island-wide delivery from Charlottetown — job sites, farms, and businesses in every county, placed by a crew that knows Island roads and driveways.

    Outside the six provinces?

    Ask us — delivery further afield can often be arranged. Tell us the destination town in your quote request and we'll work out the full delivered price — the item, hauling, and placement — in one number.

    The bridge factor

    Every mainland load bound for PEI crosses the Confederation Bridge, and the bridge closes to high-sided vehicles 8–12 times a winter for wind. We plan around it — and if your delivery day is one of those days, we reschedule at no extra charge.

    Why delivery is quoted per job

    Distance, site access, and bridge crossings all change the hauling cost — and a 9-tonne excavator moves differently than a shed. Rather than pad a flat rate, we quote your actual delivery, so Island customers aren't paying for someone else's long haul.
